lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA by setting body-text contrast to at least 3:1 against every background.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Presented quarterly findings to the head of product and two design teams; three of the top five recommended fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA), Tableau
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is not standard on US or Canadian résumés and can introduce bias.

items.says: Remove nationality.
items.because: It is less useful than work-authorization status and may create screening bias.

items.says: Make the portfolio URL clickable and link it directly to relevant case studies.
items.because: A general homepage is less useful.

items.says: Use the same professional identity across the résumé, portfolio, and application materials.
Confirm the contact information is current if it is not anonymized.
Use consistent date punctuation, preferably en dashes.
Consider using graduation year instead of month-level dates.
items.because: It could reduce clutter.

items.says: Add honors or relevant coursework only if genuinely differentiating.
Add the A/B test sample size and statistical confidence if available.
items.because: Four weeks alone does not show that the result was reliable.

items.says: Confirm abandonment was measured consistently across control and treatment.
Qualify the implied causation if other changes occurred during the test.
items.because: The design change may not have caused the entire reduction.

items.says: The 3:1 contrast threshold is incorrect for normal body text under WCAG 2.1 AA.
items.because: The requirement is generally 4.5:1.

items.says: Contrast alone cannot establish that the entire design system meets WCAG 2.1 AA.
items.because: AA has other applicable success criteria.

items.says: Specify which tokens, components, or products the work covered.
items.because: “Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA” is a broad compliance claim.

items.says: Include validation or audit evidence if available.
“Synthesizing” does not match the past-tense bullets or provide a clear grammatical subject.
Shorten the methodology list if space is tight.
items.because: It delays the outcome.

items.says: Identify the product or content change resulting from the research.
items.because: Research synthesis itself would not directly reduce support calls.

items.says: Give the measurement period for the 23% reduction.
Clarify whether the reduction was attributable to the resulting changes.
Add commas consistently in the list of research methods.
Clarify whether “head of product” is a formal title.
items.because: It should be capitalized only if it is.

items.says: Explain how the “top five” recommendations were ranked if you contributed to that ranking.
Describe the importance of the three shipped fixes.
items.because: The number shipped alone does not convey their importance.

items.says: Add the baseline and resulting number of tests if available.
items.because: “Doubled” is less informative without scale.

items.says: Specify how long the increase in tests was sustained.
Clarify whether you established quality controls or review standards.
items.because: Enabling non-researchers to conduct studies can raise research-quality concerns.

items.says: Add baseline and post-launch sample sizes if available.
Be careful attributing the sign-up increase to the design.
items.because: The comparison was post-launch rather than a controlled experiment.

items.says: Clarify whether you owned only the research or also influenced prioritization and design.
Consider moving this bullet above lower-impact or less rigorous bullets.
items.because: It is one of the strongest bullets.

items.says: The stated average 0–10 rating is not Net Promoter Score.
items.because: NPS subtracts the percentage of detractors from the percentage of promoters and ranges from –100 to +100.

items.says: Explain what you did to influence the improvement.
items.because: The outcome is not connected to your work.

items.says: Clarify whether 2,000 responses were collected monthly or in total.
Avoid saying you “raised” the score unless your work can be tied to the change.
Clarify your role in getting the two-way reminder implemented.
items.because: The bullet moves from your findings to the implementation.

items.says: Add the period over which missed appointments declined.
Confirm the 14% and 9% figures cover comparable patients and periods.
Soften the causal implication if other operational changes occurred.
“Writes” is in the wrong tense for this role.
items.because: The role ended in 2022.

items.says: Avoid “all patient studies” unless the templates covered every study.
Explain how setup time was measured and over what period.
Clarify your contribution if others implemented or approved the templates.
Clarify that you did not independently handle legal or ethics approval if it was outside your role.
items.because: The consent-template claim could imply that responsibility.

items.says: Use precise, respectful participant language and give the age range if relevant.
Give the period and baseline call volume behind the 30% reduction.
Clarify whether participants used assistive technologies or had accessibility needs.
items.because: That could explain what influenced the redesign.

items.says: Avoid overclaiming causality if the support environment changed concurrently.
Clarify what “Present” means for the ongoing project.
items.because: The bullets describe completed testing and outcomes.

items.says: Identify any additional environment used to prototype or test screen-reader behavior.
items.because: Figma alone may not explain how that work was done.

items.says: Ensure the portfolio provides evidence for the accessibility claims.
Specify whether the 12 participants were screen-reader users, low-vision users, or both.
items.because: The target population is central to the project’s credibility.

items.says: Identify the assistive technologies and devices used.
Clarify whether the map was a functioning accessible prototype or a simulated concept.
items.because: Figma has native accessibility limitations.

items.says: Identify the comparison used for route-finding performance.
items.because: It could have been an existing map, an earlier prototype, or a baseline attempt.

items.says: The change from 90 to 60 seconds is not a 50% improvement in time.
items.because: It is a 33% reduction in elapsed time.

items.says: Replace the vague word “improvement” with the actual completion-time measure.
Report participant variation or statistical limitations if results varied substantially.
items.because: The sample was small.

items.says: Clarify whether audio landmarks and color changes were tested separately.
items.because: Otherwise their individual effects cannot be isolated.

items.says: The increase from 65% to 85% is not 20%.
items.because: It is 20 percentage points, or approximately 31% relative increase.

items.says: Avoid repeating the preceding bullet’s intervention details without a distinct finding.
Define task success.
Consider consolidating the two outcome bullets.
items.because: They may describe the same test and intervention.

items.says: Do not imply high-contrast colors helped screen-reader-only users without supporting results.
items.because: The participant groups and results must support that conclusion.

items.says: Clarify your individual responsibilities in the team project.
items.because: Team accomplishments can be hard to attribute.

items.says: Do not emphasize Figma if other research, analytics, or implementation tools mattered more.
Specify whether phone bookings fell by 25% in volume or as a share of bookings.
Provide the baseline phone-booking volume if available.
Avoid attributing the entire decline to the redesign unless other clinic changes were ruled out.
Explain whether reducing phone bookings was an agreed success metric.
items.because: It could merely represent a shift in channel use.

items.says: Explain how the 10 participants were split between testing rounds.
Replace “hallway testing” with the actual setting or method.
items.because: The informal label is especially questionable in a healthcare context.

items.says: Define why the six issues were blocking issues.
Add any measured completion or usability improvement after the second round.
Ensure recruitment and consent followed clinic privacy requirements.
Clarify whether you wrote the handbook independently or led a team effort.
Make the handbook’s connection to later Spanish-language booking precise.
items.because: The later teams, not necessarily the handbook, produced the translation.

items.says: Mention accessibility or content-governance standards in the handbook if applicable.
List these tools only if you can discuss your practical proficiency with each.
Separate assistive technologies from general design and analytics tools.
items.because: “Screen-reader testing” is a capability or method, while VoiceOver and NVDA are tools.

items.says: Check for important research, analytics, survey, or qualitative-analysis tools to add.
items.because: The tools list is sparse for a senior researcher.

items.says: “interveiws” is misspelled.
Use consistent capitalization.
Add demonstrated strengths such as synthesis, affinity mapping, journey mapping, accessibility testing, and research enablement.
Distinguish research methods from analysis and facilitation skills.
Retain A/B testing only if you can defend your experimental design and analysis.
Lead each role with its strongest, most defensible impact bullets.
Make metric types clear throughout.
items.because: Percentages, percentage-point changes, averages, and counts differ.

items.says: Add periods, sample sizes, and baselines where they aid credibility without overloading bullets.
Distinguish causation from correlation in post-launch outcomes.
Keep verb tense consistent with completed and ongoing work.
Limit absolute and broad compliance claims to what can be supported.
Check line wrapping in the final document.
items.because: Bullets should not break awkwardly.

items.says: Account for the period after June 2025 if applying now.
items.because: The ongoing independent project may not fully explain your current professional status.
